questions.problem: Find the general solution to the matrix differential equation $\,{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}]x(t).$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a decoupled system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & \lambda \end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}],
$$

the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\lambda t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Since the matrix of our differential equation is diagonal, the system is decoupled. 

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t/4}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t/4},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear differential equations given by

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]x(t).
$$

Given that the solution to the system can be written as

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ a\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ a\end{aligned}]t{e}^{5t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ b\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $a+b?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}].$

Since $A$ is upper-triangular, the repeated eigenvalue is $\lambda =5$ (of multiplicity two).
For this eigenvalue, we get 

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
$v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda $ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $v$, the solution of the system of differential equations is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}\,),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

To find $w,$ we solve the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}5-5 & 2 \\ 0 & 5-5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0{w}_{1}+2{w}_{2}=1 \\ 0{w}_{1}+0{w}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

$$
{w}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

The variable ${w}_{1}$ is a free variable. Setting ${w}_{1}=0,$ we get 

$$
w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]t{e}^{5t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, we see that $a=0,b=\frac{1}{2},$ and $a+b=\frac{1}{2}.$

questions.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}].$

Since $A$ is upper-triangular, the repeated eigenvalue is $\lambda =-2$ (of multiplicity two).
For this eigenvalue, we get 

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
$v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda $ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $v$, the solution to the system of differential equations is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

To find $w,$ we solve the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}-2+2 & 0 \\ 5 & -2+2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0{w}_{1}+0{w}_{2}=0 \\ 5{w}_{1}+0{w}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

$$
{w}_{1}=\frac{1}{5}.
$$

The variable ${w}_{2}$ is a free variable. Setting ${w}_{2}=0,$  we get

$$
w=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5} \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{-2t}+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5} \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Now, we need to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial condition $x(0)=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(0) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{c}_{2}}{5} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{c}_{2}}{5} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]t{e}^{-2t}+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}. \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]t{e}^{-2t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-2t} \\ (2+5t){e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the solution to the system can be written as

$$

$$

what is the value of $a+b?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}].$

Since $A$ is lower-triangular, the repeated eigenvalue is $\lambda =-1$ (of multiplicity two).
For this eigenvalue, we get 

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
$v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda $ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $v$, the solution of the system of differential equations is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}\,),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

To find $w,$ we solve the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}-1-(-1) & 0 \\ 3 & -1-(-1)\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0{w}_{1}+0{w}_{2}=0 \\ 3{w}_{1}+0{w}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

$$
{w}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

The variable ${w}_{2}$ is a free variable. Setting ${w}_{2}=0,$ we get 

$$
w=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{-t}+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, we see that $a=0,b=\frac{1}{3},$ and $a+b=\frac{1}{3}.$

questions.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -6 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}].$

Since $A$ is upper-triangular, the repeated eigenvalue is $\lambda =-3$ (of multiplicity two).
For this eigenvalue, we get 

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}0 & -6 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
$v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda $ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $v$, the solution to the system of differential equations is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

To find $w,$ we solve the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}-3-(-3) & -6 \\ 0 & -3-(-3)\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & -6 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0{w}_{1}-6{w}_{2}=1 \\ 0{w}_{1}+0{w}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

$$
{w}_{2}=-\frac{1}{6}.
$$

The variable ${w}_{1}$ is a free variable. Setting ${w}_{1}=0,$  we get

$$
w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]t{e}^{-3t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Now, we need to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial condition $x(0)=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(0) & =[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ -\frac{{c}_{2}}{6}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ -\frac{{c}_{2}}{6}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}]t{e}^{-3t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}]t{e}^{-3t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(1-12t){e}^{-3t} \\ 2\,{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
